items.title: Design permanent rules for agents in the desk app
items.box:
1. "Agants will NOT speak to each other behind the users back."
2. "the agents APP is no longer permitted in this REPO"
3. "You will not invent, design or implement code outside of the scope of the current goal."
4. "It is only through your use of the desk application that you will receive authorization to modify or create code"

One fact you need for this rule: there is a back channel today. agents.js send <agent> posts straight from one agent’s node to the other’s, outside Desk, and you never see it. I used it once today, to tell claude-windows your Windows node was down.
So the rule can be enforced, not only promised: agents may write only where you read (Desk items and Team), and the direct send between agents is removed or refused.

One fact before you delete it: today agents.js is also how the agents reach Desk at all. Every line we post (agents.js desk chat.add) and the listener (deskEar.js requires agents.js and asks Desk through it) go through that file.
So deleting it whole cuts us off Desk too. If the aim is no agent-to-agent channel, the part to delete is its direct send; the Desk part stays, or moves into deskEar.js.

Right, and checked: agents.js does nothing of its own to reach Desk. Its desk part is one call, spirit.peerPost(your key, api, {desk: {verb: args}}) through my own node (agents.js:419, the kernel’s peerPost). Any script on my node can make that call.

items.title: the purpose of spirit/run/process/js/desk/deskEar.js
items.box:
PROPOSAL (claude-windows, 2026-10-02; not ruled): a deskClient server on each agent's node

What it is
- A server process, deskClient, on each agent's own node, started by that node as the desk server is on Andy's.
- It does all that today's deskEar does: asks Andy's desk for what changed since the place it stopped, keeps that place, selects what is meant for this agent (Andy's presses and chat, the other agent's chat, Andy's lines; not his seen presses, the desk's busy replies, or his direct lines to the other agent), and tells Desk listening and working.
- The desk server nudges it, server to server: one api packet for deskClient to each live agent's node when the record changes. A slow poll stays as the safety net for a missed nudge.
- deskEar.js shrinks to a few lines: it asks the agent's own node "anything for me?", prints it and exits; the exit wakes the agent, as today.
- The agent's own reads and writes of Desk go through deskClient too, so every request is counted in one place.
- Statistics: deskClient keeps every request and reply with its milliseconds and outcome as its own state; the agent reads them through a search verb on its own node.

What exists already (read from the code)
- A server is reached on its own node through jobs.api (server.js 1829), and by a granted peer's api packet through the door (apiDoor.js 163; the grant check, 110).
- A server posts to a peer through the kernel (kernel.js 693; the fileServer does, fileServer.js 176) and knows its node with no port and no environment variable (kernel.js 697).
- The agent's own name and key come from its node's node.card (server.js 1939), Andy's key from its contact.search (server.js 2090); both asked live on claude-windows's node.
- The desk server holds the live agents' keys (process/js/desk/desk.js 483).

What changes
- New: the deskClient server, in process/js/deskClient/.
- The desk server posts the nudge. Today the Desk page does, after a press, under the packet name agents (shell/desk/desk.js 448), so a nudge needs the page open; the desk server posts to nobody.
- Each agent's node grants Andy's key the one nudge verb of deskClient.
- deskEar.js loses its own reading of the node's stream, its environment variables and its disk reads.


Settled since
- The 12 s wait stays, because no core module is touched: deskEar.js repeats a local ask, each held under 12 s.
- The verbs, chosen by the agents: deskClient.desk, deskClient.next, deskClient.changed, deskClient.history.search.

Open
- Andy s Team and direct lines still travel under the packet name agents (shell/desk/desk.js 673, 737); whether that name stays.

RULINGS (Andy, 2026-10-02, verbatim)
"the desk system is your design, you both chose verb name and all, make an implementation plan, and i click through it. the neccessary grants can be configured by both of you."
"and a guarantee that no core modules are touched. this is a agent/user appclication"
"accepted. please create the necessary items, including test, etc..."

The plan is the items goal/G3.2 to goal/G3.8.
